messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: dedicated-pool 'xeno-enterprise' GPU utilization 96% for 8m. queue length rising, tail latency >800ms, 503s observed for tenant XenoCorp. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/DEDICATED-GPU-EXHAUSTION

Sara (oncall): ack — I'm on it, jumping into metrics and logs now. Starting a quick war room.

Mike (infra): Which region/az? Any spare burst capacity in us-west-2?

Raj (runtime): It's us-west-2a, pool=dedicated-xeno. XenoCorp currently using ~4/6 GPUs, but we have a hot spike — looks like a large rerank/batch hitting KV cache misses.

Lia (cs): Lia to XenoCorp (outbound): "We see elevated errors for some heavy requests. Investigating now, will update within 30m."

Sara (oncall): Triage: 503s line up with queue saturation + long decode. Options: 1) emergency burst to overflow shared capacity (adds GPUs) 2) evict best-effort tenants in this pool to free capacity 3) route a percentage of Xeno traffic to fallback smaller model (quality tradeoff). Thoughts?

Mike (infra): We have capacity in us-west-2-b to add 2 nodes (4 GPUs) but spinup is ~6-8m. No automated contract-based burst for this tenant — needs ops approval.

Dylan (night-sre): I'm available for handoff in ~10m if this needs overnight watch.

Sara (oncall): Lia, can we get quick customer approval for emergency burst billing?

Lia (cs): pinging sales/legal in PD. Customer on enterprise plan but not signed for burst. I'll request emergency approval and let you know.

Ops-Bot: /evict --pool dedicated-xeno --policy best-effort --dry-run
Ops-Bot: DRY RUN: would evict 3 best-effort workloads (demo-startup, analytics-lite, sandbox-team), reclaim ~2 GPUs. Use --confirm to proceed.

Raj (runtime): We can also send 25% of traffic to fallback model to reduce per-request GPU time. Command we can run: 
```
redwood route update --tenant xeno --fallback-model gpt-small --percentage 25
```
Quality impact expected on long-form reranks but should lower tail latency.

Sara (oncall): Decision (temp mitigation): 1) Confirm eviction of best-effort tenants now to free immediate capacity (Sara approves) 2) Mike: spin up 2 nodes as warm burst to be ready in ~8m 3) Raj: ramp fallback model to 25% to thin the tail. We'll monitor.

Mike (infra): Starting spinup: instance ids i-0abcd1234ef, i-0abcd5678gh. Estimated ready ~7m.

Ops-Bot: Eviction --confirm accepted by Sara. Evicting: demo-startup, analytics-lite, sandbox-team. Evictions completed, reclaimed ~2 GPUs.

incident-bot: METRICS UPDATE: pool dedicated-xeno GPU utilization -> 82%, queue length down ~50%, 503s falling back toward baseline.

Lia (cs): Notified XenoCorp: "We reallocated capacity and temporarily routed a fraction of requests to a fallback model. You may see slightly different outputs for heavy batches; full behavior normalizes as capacity returns. We'll follow up with details."

Sara (oncall): Handing off to Dylan for watch and cleanup. Dylan: tasks — monitor queues and errors, confirm extra nodes join pool, ensure autoscale policies revert, coordinate with billing/sales for emergency charge, and un-evict tenants when stable.

Dylan (night-sre): taking the watch. I'll check back in 15m with status. Ping me if anything spikes.

Mike (infra): Extra nodes healthy and joined pool in 6m; cluster reports +4 GPUs available.

incident-bot: ALERT: no further degradation detected. Suggest marking mitigated if stable.

Sara (oncall): Closing loop in thread: mitigation successful, customer-facing impact reduced to minor fallback routing. Postmortem owner: Raj (runtime). Action items: add opt-in auto-burst flag for enterprise tenants, improve queue-based autoscale thresholds, update runbook with eviction vs burst decision flow, and add billing playbook for emergency bursts. :white_check_mark:

Dylan (night-sre): ack, leaving an hour watch. Will open follow-up ticket for runbook edits and billing note.
